clue.text: Fellow politician with non-standard dialect difficult to understand

parts.note: CO is the prefix for a partner or fellow, as in co-pilot or co-worker
an MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: a dialect that is non-standard departs from the usual form, so its letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A colleague in parliament speaks in such a strange regional dialect that nobody can follow them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-standard' rearranges DIALECT into LICATED, which follows CO and MP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something complicated is intricate and involved, hence hard to follow or grasp.

clue.text: One operates underground dog races, showing front

parts.note: a collie is a breed of sheepdog

indicators.note: only the front letter of the word races is shown, so just its first letter is used

explanation.surface: Someone working below ground somehow makes dogs race, putting on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A collier is a coal miner, a worker whose job lies down in the pits.

clue.text: State of America that's up in east

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word that is up is read from bottom to top, so the letters of America's abbreviation run backwards

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Asks which American state is the one that rises in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's up' signals reading upwards, which in a down clue means backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is one of the fifty US states, in the north-east corner of New England.

clue.text: Pound put on game, often losing? Sucker

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece put on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: to lam is to beat or pound someone
prey is game, the hunted animal that usually loses out to its hunter

explanation.surface: A gambler stakes money on a game they usually lose: what a sucker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'often losing' describes the hunted creature, not a gambler.
explanation.definitionFit: The lamprey is an eel-like fish that clings to prey with a round sucking mouth, so it is literally a sucker.

clue.text: It's starchy dumpling served in wine

indicators.note: something served in a glass of wine sits inside it, so one word is placed within the other

parts.note: cava is Spanish sparkling wine
a dumpling, like an ass, can mean a dim or silly person

explanation.surface: A stodgy dumpling comes served in a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dumpling' looks like food but is a dim, plump person; 'served in' places it after the wine's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassava is a tropical root crop rich in starch, the source of tapioca.

clue.text: Eatery closed after vermin cited in short hearing

indicators.note: things cited in a hearing are brought up within it, so one set of letters goes inside another
a short word loses its last letter

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing

indicators.note: closed comes after vermin, so its letters follow

parts.note: a rat is vermin
a door pushed to is closed, so to can mean closed

explanation.surface: A restaurant is shut down after rats are mentioned in a brief court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts TRIAL to TRIA, and 'cited in' puts RATTO inside it after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an informal Italian restaurant, a kind of place to eat.

clue.text: Scottish king getting George to replace fourth and fifth cell

indicators.note: the shortened George takes the place of the fourth and fifth letters of the king's name

parts.note: Duncan was a king of Scotland, famously murdered in Macbeth

explanation.surface: A Scottish monarch has a George take over two of his ranks and ends up in a cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace fourth and fifth' swaps CA, the fourth and fifth letters of DUNCAN, for GEO.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is an underground prison cell, as found beneath castles.

clue.text: Fabled Captain ran the manoeuvres east of Tennessee maybe

indicators.note: in an across clue the piece east of another sits to its right, so it comes after

parts.note: Tennessee Williams the playwright is one example of someone named Williams

indicators.note: the words ran the are moved about and manoeuvred into a new order

explanation.surface: A legendary sea captain steers his ship east of Tennessee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvres' signals the anagram and 'east of' puts it after the surname. Tennessee looks like a US state but is the playwright's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: William Shatner played Captain James T. Kirk of the Enterprise in Star Trek, a captain of legend.

clue.text: Cleaner's house programme

parts.note: Windsor is the royal house of the British monarchy
a soap is a soap opera, a type of television programme

explanation.surface: The cleaning lady's home-improvement TV show.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is a link joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Windsor soap is a traditional brown scented toilet soap, something you wash with.

clue.text: See 7
Novices stuck in middle of arete needing sustenance

indicators.note: the novices are stuck inside, so their letters go within the other piece
only the middle part of the word arete is used, without its outer letters

parts.note: freshmen are first-year students, newcomers or novices

explanation.surface: Beginner climbers stranded halfway along a mountain ridge need food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' drops the outer letters of ARETE, a sharp mountain ridge, and 'stuck in' places the novices within what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Refreshment is food and drink that restores strength, a form of nourishment.

clue.text: Taking a turn, Welshman holds one born yesterday?

indicators.note: a word taking a turn is turned round, so its letters are read backwards
the Welshman holds the other piece, so it goes inside his name

parts.note: Evan is a typical Welsh man's name
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A Welshman taking a stroll keeps hold of someone very gullible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts I inside EVAN for EVIAN, and 'Taking a turn' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wasn't born yesterday is worldly, so being born yesterday means being innocent and gullible.

clue.text: A ref's to be organised for Sunday fixture?

indicators.note: the referee's letters are to be organised, so they are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A referee is still to be assigned for a Sunday football match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixture' suggests a sports match, but here it means a regular feature of the British Sunday lunch table.
explanation.definitionFit: Roast beef is the traditional British Sunday lunch, a weekly regular on the table.

clue.text: Unkempt, small Dutch footballer advancing very powerfully

indicators.note: the musical marking moves forward one place inside the footballer's name

parts.note: Johan Cruyff was a famous Dutch footballer
FF, fortissimo, is the musical direction for very loud or powerful

explanation.surface: A scruffy little Dutch footballer charges forward with great power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advancing' moves the FF of CRUYFF forward past the Y to give CRUFFY.
explanation.definitionFit: Scruffy means shabby and untidy in appearance, the same as dishevelled.

clue.text: Youngster went ahead with golf, cutting pitch

indicators.note: the earlier pieces cut into the word for pitch, so they sit inside it

parts.note: to fling is to pitch or throw
led means went ahead, at the front
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A young player went in front at golf, cutting across the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' puts LEDG inside FLING after its F. 'Pitch' reads as a sports field but is a throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A fledgling is a young bird just able to fly, and by extension any inexperienced newcomer.

clue.text: Order class design catalogue

definitions.meaning: to ... items is to class or sort them
to ... is to plan or design, as music is ...
to ... a collection is to list or catalogue it

explanation.surface: An instruction to set up a catalogue for a design class.
explanation.walkthrough: Four verbs side by side, each a sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of these four verbs covers a way of setting things out systematically or planning them.

clue.text: Ask for horseman to eject Republican Scotsman following king

indicators.note: the cut-down horseman comes after the king, so its letters follow

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: the horseman is made to eject the others, so their letters are thrown out of him

parts.note: an equestrian is a horse rider
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A rider is asked to throw out a Republican Scot who comes after the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eject' takes the R and IAN out of EQUESTRIAN, leaving EQUEST.
explanation.definitionFit: To request something is to ask for it politely.

clue.text: A couple of pints and in another world? Blur perhaps

parts.note: a quart is two pints
ET, the extra-terrestrial, lives in another world

explanation.surface: Two pints down and feeling far away, everything is a blur.
explanation.walkthrough: Blur is the 1990s Britpop band, not hazy vision.
explanation.definitionFit: Blur were a band with four members, so they are an example of a foursome of musicians.

clue.text: Dick's investment fund

definitions.meaning: dick is slang for a detective, one who tracks down suspects
a fund that follows a stock-market index

explanation.surface: A man called Dick's savings scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is a link joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A detective trails suspects, and an index fund trails the market, so both follow something.

clue.text: Little snog? As spoken by drunk rather lacking in taste

indicators.note: a drunk slurs the s sounds into sh, so the words come out sounding like the answer

parts.note: a wee kiss is a little snog, wee being Scottish for small

explanation.surface: A drunk asks for a quick kiss, which turns out rather tasteless.
explanation.walkthrough: A snog is British slang for a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Weakish means somewhat weak, as with diluted tea or a thin drink without much flavour.

clue.text: I'm unhappy with old English semi being converted

indicators.note: a semi being converted is remodelled, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is miserable about their old English semi-detached house being converted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being converted' rearranges SEMI into ISME. A semi is a British semi-detached house.
explanation.definitionFit: Woe is me is an old-fashioned lament, a way of saying how miserable one feels.

clue.text: Ape's current temper not improving outwardly

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: not removes the next letters from the word for temper

parts.note: to temper is to mitigate, make milder

indicators.note: only the outside letters of the word improving are used

explanation.surface: A monkey's present bad mood shows no sign of getting better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outwardly' gives IG from IMPROVING, and 'not' removes it from MITIGATE, leaving MITATE. 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to copy or mimic them.

clue.text: Pop's diversity seen in vocal duet occasionally

indicators.note: the diversity is seen inside the other letters, so it goes within them
only occasional letters of the words vocal duet are taken, every other one

parts.note: a range is a varied selection, a diversity

explanation.surface: A pop group's variety shows itself now and then in a sung duet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes every other letter of VOCAL DUET, starting with the second, and 'seen in' places the diversity after the first. 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop is a fizzy soft drink, and orangeade is one such sweet carbonated drink.

clue.text: Unknown hacks into a German website

indicators.note: the unknown hacks into the other word, getting inside it

parts.note: eine is German for a
Z is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An anonymous hacker breaks into a German website.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hacks into' puts Z inside EINE after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: An e-zine is an online magazine, published on a website.

clue.text: Runner with a temperature gets leave of absence

parts.note: a river runs, and the Exe is a river in Devon

explanation.surface: An athlete with a fever is granted time off.
explanation.walkthrough: Runner is a crossword convention for a river; the Exe is in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An exeat is formal permission for a student to be absent from school or college.

clue.text: Player's prank in former times: spraying water

indicators.note: the prank goes in the word for former times

parts.note: the past is former times
a trick is a prank

indicators.note: water spraying is scattered about, so its letters are mixed

explanation.surface: An actor's old practical joke was squirting people with water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the prank inside former times, and 'spraying' signals the anagram of water. 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Patrick Stewart is an actor, a player on stage and screen, best known as Captain Picard.

clue.text: See 22
Insect, the thing over car plate that's seen from behind VW

indicators.note: seen from behind, the letters are read backwards from the far end
the thing goes over the plate, and seen from behind it comes first

parts.note: a reg is a car registration plate
it means the thing
the Beetle is the famous Volkswagen car

explanation.surface: An insect spotted on a car's number plate, seen from behind a Volkswagen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen from behind' reverses REGIT to give TIGER.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger beetle is a fast predatory beetle, a kind of insect.
